meta.title: Who really said "You will continue to suffer if you have an emotional reaction to everything that is said to you. True power is sitting back and observing everything with logic. True power is restraint"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: No — Bruce Lee never said this. Quote Investigator and PolitiFact trace it to an anonymous 2016 tweet; the Bruce Lee credit only appeared in 2018.

answer.label: Not Bruce Lee — an anonymous social-media aphorism
answer.authorDates: Full wording first documented online in 2016; not by Bruce Lee (1940–1973)
answer.sourceLine: This is a modern internet aphorism with no author. Quote Investigator traces the complete wording to a March 2016 tweet posted with no attribution, built from fragments circulating since 2009; the Bruce Lee credit did not appear until October 2018. PolitiFact rated the Bruce Lee attribution “False,” and the Bruce Lee Foundation confirmed it has no proof he said it.

source.heading: Where the line actually comes from

docMeta.dd: Bruce Lee (also Warren Buffett; Sylvester McNutt III)

source.excerpt: You will continue to suffer if you have an emotional reaction to everything that is said to you. True power is sitting back and observing everything with logic. True power is restraint. If words control you that means everyone else can control you. Breathe and allow things to pass.
trail: Pre-2016 fragments. Quote Investigator finds pieces of the saying on Twitter as far back as 2009, with “True power is restraint” tweeted by March 2011 — well before any celebrity attribution.

Full wording, unattributed, 2016. The complete passage was tweeted without any author by Cindy Flores on 24 March 2016, per Quote Investigator; the Bruce Lee credit did not surface until October 2018.
No evidence from Bruce Lee. PolitiFact rated the attribution “False”; the Bruce Lee Foundation’s licensing director said she had no proof Lee said it.
source.excerptNote: The full form that circulates online; the “True power is restraint” fragment appears in tweets as early as March 2011, per Quote Investigator.
source.rightsNote: The exact wording is an anonymous modern aphorism with no identifiable author or source work, so no copyright status can be responsibly asserted. It is not a documented Bruce Lee text, and there is no known original publication to date.

author.name: Bruce Lee
author.heading: Who the quote is pinned on
author.bio: Bruce Lee was a Hong Kong–American martial artist, actor, and founder of Jeet Kune Do whose real writings (collected in Striking Thoughts and Tao of Jeet Kune Do) made him a magnet for feel-good aphorisms he never wrote. He died in 1973 — more than four decades before this saying was first pinned on him online. His actual philosophy prized flowing adaptability (“be water”) rather than the stoic emotional restraint this internet quote preaches.

misattribution.heading: How this ended up on Bruce Lee
misattribution.intro: This is a textbook social-media aphorism: it circulated anonymously for years, then got retro-fitted onto famous names to lend it authority. It has been credited to at least three different people.

items.why: PolitiFact found no source connecting the words to Lee, who died in 1973; the credit did not appear until October 2018, per Quote Investigator.
A @WarrenBuffettHQ tweet spread a Buffett attribution in August 2018; Quote Investigator calls it unconvincing, with no link to anything Buffett wrote or said.
The author/coach tweeted the line on 14 January 2018, but that is years after the unattributed 2016 version, so it is a relay rather than an origin, per Quote Investigator.

misattribution.truthLine: The honest answer: nobody famous. The full wording first appears in an unattributed 2016 tweet, assembled from fragments online since 2009 — per Quote Investigator.

context.heading: Why it sticks to Bruce Lee
lead: The saying preaches stoic emotional detachment — don’t react, observe with logic, let words pass. That reads as vaguely “Eastern” wisdom, which makes Bruce Lee a frictionless host for it, even though his own signature teaching (“be water”) is about adaptive flow, not iron restraint.

Because the line genuinely resonates, people rarely question the byline — and a famous name travels further than “anonymous.” That is exactly the mechanism that turns a good tweet into a fake Bruce Lee quote.
context.pull: Nobody famous said it — it’s a 2016 tweet with no author.
